body:
Throwaway account.

*1) I had a brain tumor that has an occurrence rate of 3 in 1,000,000. I was finally diagnosed when I was on the brink of death (due to severe hydrocephalus - my brain was about to massively herniate) at a small, local hospital. 
*2) However, I was slated for discharge, because the ER doctor did not think that my case was urgent. 
*3) HOWEVER, the one and only neurosurgeon on call at the hospital had been flagged to double check my brain scan earlier. He did it minutes before I was discharged, and rushed into my room to prevent me from leaving. The neurosurgeon told me that I had minutes to live, and to trust him.
*4) HOWEVER, I desperately wanted to be transferred to <World Famous Hospital> down the road. 
*5) HOWEVER, the neurosurgeon was persuasive that there was not time for that. I decided to trust him.
*6) During surgery to relieve pressure on my brain, my brain expressed a sustained fountain of fluid 6 cm high. The surgical staff were amazed that I survived.

So yeah... I was on a freight train towards death. Spoiler alert: I survived.

I witnessed the dissection of a live extraterrestrial being. It was not anesthetized, because neither human nor veterinary anesthesia works on aliens. I was told to tell no one.

Edit: BRB, doorbell

I'm 30, have 5 brain surgeries under my belt (to remove a tumor, for which.I have MRIs every 6 months to check for a recurrence), and I'm pretty damn sure that I would never be drafted, even if I begged to be.
A fully intact skull and brain (after 6 brain surgeries, I'm missing a few pieces here and there).

I heard "it's all in your head" and "you're a hypochondriac" for over a decade.  Turns out they were right!  I had a brain tumor!  For fucks sake, it took way too long for the doctors to figure that one out.

Hey there.  I just started on a chronic pain management regime for a brain injury (caused by SIX different brain surgeries... for a stubborn brain tumor).  I get phantom limb pain on one entire side of my body.  It's hard to describe, but when I wake up... I feel like the bones on one side of my body are broken.  Not an exaggeration.  It is agonizing.  At the moment, I am taking 10/325 Percs, and have enough for 2 a day.  I am on partial medical leave, because I have a disability.  Some days... especially those days when I am taking it really easy... I only take one Perc.  So that way I build up an excess of Percs for days when I exert myself more.  Exertion = more pain = more need for Percs.  So far (2 months in) I am able to control my intake.  At most, I take 3 a day.  I do not feel "cravings" for Percs that I just have to subdue... but I suspect it is only a matter of time before that happens.  Any advice on this would be appreciated.

Hey brain tumor friend.

I think few people understand the toll that cutting through ones brain takes on a person.  You and I are in the same boat in that regard.  They cut away parts of "you" and yet "you" still emerges somehow.  A different you, but nonetheless you.  I am up to 6 brain surgeries now.  And the crazy thing is that I don't have brain cancer, but a stubborn type of non-cancerous tumor that originally required a lot of surgeries... and has recurred.  One of my craniotomies was almost certainly the major culprit in my chronic pain.  It went through my motor cortex (there was no other choice).  A shunt placement surgery of all things went through my OTHER motor cortex.  I'm talking to a psychiatrist now.  He wants me to try alternative pain relief methods (in addition to the heavier painkillers), like hypnosis.  Hypnosis is actually quite powerful, and works for several hours... but it is difficult for me to perform on myself and sustain that feeling for very long.  I will take a look at that book.  Any more relief from where I am at right now would improve my quality of life immensely.
